objects.description: Configuration for starting a streaming session, including video resolution/FPS/bitrate, audio layout, supported codecs, display timing, colorimetry, encryption options, and remote input AES keys/IVs.
Linked-list node describing a buffer segment of a video frame, carrying a pointer, size, and optional codec-specific buffer type for IDR units.
A video decode submission unit aggregating one frame's buffers and timing/telemetry, including frame type, RTP timestamp, receive/queue/presentation times, and HDR/colorspace hints.
Callback vtable the client provides for the video decoder/renderer, including setup/start/stop/cleanup and submission of decode units, plus capability flags.
Parameters required to configure an Opus multistream decoder for the negotiated audio stream, including sample rate, layout, and channel mapping.
Callback vtable the client provides for audio rendering, including init/start/stop/cleanup and decode/play sample entry point, plus capability flags.
Callback bundle for connection lifecycle, logging, controller haptics/LED, connection status, HDR mode, and motion event state updates.
Describes the target host and negotiated server properties including address, server info strings, RTSP session URL, and codec mode support bitmask.
Read-only cumulative counters for RTP audio stream packets, FEC activity, out-of-sequence, and invalid packets.
Read-only cumulative counters for RTP video stream packets, FEC activity, out-of-sequence, and invalid packets.
Container for HDR mastering/display metadata including primaries, white point, display luminance bounds, and optional content/display light level fields.

Singly linked-list node representing an application entry parsed from XML. Each node holds an app name, an integer ID, and a pointer to the next node. Used by xml_applist() to return a list of available applications. Memory ownership and lifetime are not documented here and must be inferred from the implementation elsewhere.

Singly linked-list node representing a display mode parsed from XML. Contains resolution (height, width) and refresh rate in Hz, plus a next pointer for list chaining. Populated by xml_modelist(). Memory allocation and deallocation policy are not specified here.

Holds connection and capability information for a GameStream (GFE/NVIDIA Shield) server discovered or configured by Moonlight Embedded. Fields include server versioning, GPU type, pairing state, display modes, server information, and HTTP/HTTPS ports. Some member types (PDISPLAY_MODE, SERVER_INFORMATION) are defined externally in included headers.
Built-in C type referenced by the API; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.
Built-in C type referenced by the API; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.

Pointer to a C string containing the most recent or current error message for the library. The header only declares the symbol; its storage and lifetime are defined elsewhere. Treat as a read-only pointer to a null-terminated string. If not set by the implementation at some point, it may be NULL.

Heap-allocated buffer container for HTTP responses with a pointer to the data (memory) and its size in bytes. PHTTP_DATA is a pointer alias. Intended to be created with http_create_data(), filled by http_request(), and released with http_free_data().

Opaque holder for an OpenSSL certificate/key bundle generated by this module. It contains an X509 certificate, its corresponding private key, and a PKCS#12 container. Lifetime management is manual: use mkcert_free() to release resources. Note: X509, EVP_PKEY, and PKCS12 are OpenSSL types declared elsewhere.
Typedef alias to a pointer to CERT_KEY_PAIR. Provided for Windows-style naming convenience; points directly to a CERT_KEY_PAIR instance.

PLENTRY is referenced as a parameter type to gs_sps_fix but is not defined in this header. It likely comes from Limelight.h and represents a parsed SPS (Sequence Parameter Set) or a generic bitstream entry structure. Details are unknown here.
Alias for an unsigned 8-bit integer pointer used as an output buffer parameter. It is a standard type from <stdint.h>, not defined in this header.
Alias for an unsigned 32-bit integer pointer used as an output offset parameter. It is a standard type from <stdint.h>, not defined in this header.

functions.name: LiGetLaunchUrlQueryParameters
functions.description: Returns a library-owned query string to append to /launch and /resume URLs to enable extended functionality with Sunshine hosts. The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned string (owned by the library).
Intended to be appended to /launch and /resume query parameter strings.

functions.name: LiInitializeStreamConfiguration
functions.description: Zero-initializes a STREAM_CONFIGURATION structure allocated by the caller on stack or heap. Use before setting fields to ensure a known baseline.
requirements: streamConfig must be a valid, writable pointer to an allocated STREAM_CONFIGURATION.

functions.name: LiInitializeVideoCallbacks
functions.description: Zero-initializes a DECODER_RENDERER_CALLBACKS structure allocated by the caller. Use prior to filling callback pointers and capabilities.
requirements: drCallbacks must be a valid, writable pointer to an allocated DECODER_RENDERER_CALLBACKS.

functions.name: LiInitializeAudioCallbacks
functions.description: Zero-initializes an AUDIO_RENDERER_CALLBACKS structure allocated by the caller. Use prior to filling callback pointers and capabilities.
requirements: arCallbacks must be a valid, writable pointer to an allocated AUDIO_RENDERER_CALLBACKS.

functions.name: LiInitializeConnectionCallbacks
functions.description: Zero-initializes a CONNECTION_LISTENER_CALLBACKS structure allocated by the caller. Use prior to filling listener callbacks.
requirements: clCallbacks must be a valid, writable pointer to an allocated CONNECTION_LISTENER_CALLBACKS.

functions.name: LiInitializeServerInformation
functions.description: Zero-initializes a SERVER_INFORMATION structure allocated by the caller. Use before setting server address and info fields.
requirements: serverInfo must be a valid, writable pointer to an allocated SERVER_INFORMATION.

functions.name: LiStartConnection
functions.signature: int LiStartConnection(PSERVER_INFORMATION serverInfo, PSTREAM_CONFIGURATION streamConfig, PCONNECTION_LISTENER_CALLBACKS clCallbacks, PDECODER_RENDERER_CALLBACKS drCallbacks, PAUDIO_RENDERER_CALLBACKS arCallbacks, void* renderContext, int drFlags, void* audioContext, int arFlags);
functions.description: Begins streaming to the client using the provided server info, stream configuration, and optional callback sets for connection, video, and audio. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure. Not thread-safe.
requirements: This function is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently with itself or LiStopConnection().
serverInfo and streamConfig must point to initialized structures (use initialization helpers).
Callback structs (clCallbacks, drCallbacks, arCallbacks) are optional; pass NULL to use defaults or set individual members to NULL to omit specific callbacks.
renderContext/audioContext and drFlags/arFlags are passed through to renderer callbacks as provided.
Caller must ensure any provided callbacks adhere to their documented semantics (e.g., non-blocking if CAPABILITY_DIRECT_SUBMIT is set).

functions.name: LiStopConnection
functions.description: Stops streaming. May be invoked after a successful LiStartConnection(). Not thread-safe.
requirements: This function is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently with LiStartConnection() or itself.
Does not trigger ConnListenerConnectionTerminated() as a result of calling this function (per callback docs).

functions.name: LiInterruptConnection
functions.description: Asynchronously interrupts a pending LiStartConnection() call to abort initialization.
requirements: Do not start another connection until the interrupted LiStartConnection() call returns.
May cause ConnListenerStageFailed() during initialization, but not guaranteed.

functions.name: LiGetStageName
functions.description: Returns a stable, user-visible string name for an initialization stage code. Useful for displaying progress based on ConnListenerStage* callbacks.
requirements: stage should be a STAGE_* constant. Unknown values may return an implementation-defined string.

functions.name: LiGetEstimatedRttInfo
functions.description: Obtains an ENet-based estimate of current RTT and its variance to the host PC. Returns true on success. Only valid while a connection using ENet control is established.
requirements: Must be called only between LiStartConnection() and LiStopConnection().
Fails if the GFE version does not use ENet for control or the ENet peer is not connected.
estimatedRtt and estimatedRttVariance must be valid writable pointers.

functions.name: LiSendMouseMoveEvent
functions.description: Queues a relative mouse movement event to the remote server.
requirements: deltaX and deltaY are relative motion in device-independent units; range limited by short.
An active connection must exist for the event to be delivered (implicit).

functions.name: LiSendMousePositionEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendMousePositionEvent(short x, short y, short referenceWidth, short referenceHeight);
functions.description: Queues an absolute mouse position update transformed from a reference plane of size referenceWidth x referenceHeight. Intended for absolute pointing (e.g., touchscreens).
requirements: Absolute positioning may not work reliably on GFE < 3.20.
x and y are in the coordinate space of the specified reference plane; referenceWidth and referenceHeight should be positive.
Absolute mouse motion is often incompatible with many games; avoid as default for mice.

functions.name: LiSendMouseMoveAsMousePositionEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendMouseMoveAsMousePositionEvent(short deltaX, short deltaY, short referenceWidth, short referenceHeight);
functions.description: Sends relative motion as an absolute position by updating an internal virtual cursor tracked across calls. Helps avoid OS mouse acceleration effects when only accelerated input is available.
requirements: Do not call concurrently with LiSendMousePositionEvent(); these two functions must not be invoked concurrently due to shared virtual cursor state.
referenceWidth and referenceHeight should describe the target coordinate plane and be positive.
Shares the same limitations as LiSendMousePositionEvent() regarding game compatibility.

functions.name: LiSendTouchEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendTouchEvent(uint8_t eventType, uint32_t pointerId, float x, float y, float pressureOrDistance, float contactAreaMajor, float contactAreaMinor, uint16_t rotation);
functions.description: Sends a multi-touch event to Sunshine hosts using normalized coordinates and extended touch parameters (pressure/distance, contact area, rotation). Returns LI_ERR_UNSUPPORTED if the host does not support touch events.
requirements: eventType must be one of LI_TOUCH_EVENT_* constants.
pointerId must uniquely identify an active touch and remain constant across its down/move/up/cancel sequence.
x and y are normalized device coordinates in [0.0, 1.0] over the video area.
pressureOrDistance is 0.0–1.0 for touch pressure; for hover, 1.0–0.0 represents far-to-near distance; 0.0 may indicate unknown values as documented.
contactAreaMajor/minor are in normalized coordinates; use 0.0 if unknown; for circles set major==minor.
rotation is degrees from vertical in Y (0..360) or LI_ROT_UNKNOWN.
Returns LI_ERR_UNSUPPORTED if unsupported; feature can be pre-checked via LiGetHostFeatureFlags() and LI_FF_PEN_TOUCH_EVENTS.

functions.name: LiSendPenEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendPenEvent(uint8_t eventType, uint8_t toolType, uint8_t penButtons, float x, float y, float pressureOrDistance, float contactAreaMajor, float contactAreaMinor, uint16_t rotation, uint8_t tilt);
functions.description: Sends a pen/stylus input event with tool type, buttons, tilt, and touch-like parameters. For LI_TOUCH_EVENT_BUTTON_ONLY, position/pressure/rotation/area/tilt are ignored. Returns LI_ERR_UNSUPPORTED if unsupported by host.
requirements: eventType must be one of LI_TOUCH_EVENT_* constants; LI_TOUCH_EVENT_BUTTON_ONLY ignores position/pressure/rotation/area/tilt.
toolType should be LI_TOOL_TYPE_* (UNKNOWN/PEN/ERASER).
penButtons is a bitmask of LI_PEN_BUTTON_* flags.
x and y normalized to [0.0, 1.0]; pressure 0.0–1.0; rotation degrees or LI_ROT_UNKNOWN; tilt 0..90 degrees or LI_TILT_UNKNOWN.
Feature can be pre-checked via LiGetHostFeatureFlags() and LI_FF_PEN_TOUCH_EVENTS.

functions.name: LiSendMouseButtonEvent
functions.description: Queues a mouse button press or release event.
requirements: action must be BUTTON_ACTION_PRESS or BUTTON_ACTION_RELEASE.
button must be one of BUTTON_LEFT, BUTTON_MIDDLE, BUTTON_RIGHT, BUTTON_X1, BUTTON_X2.
An active connection must exist for delivery (implicit).

functions.name: LiSendKeyboardEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendKeyboardEvent(short keyCode, char keyAction, char modifiers);
functions.description: Queues a keyboard event using Win32 Virtual Key (VK) codes interpreted on a US English layout.
requirements: keyAction must be KEY_ACTION_DOWN or KEY_ACTION_UP.
modifiers is a bitmask of MODIFIER_* flags.
keyCode must be a valid VK code for intended behavior.

functions.name: LiSendKeyboardEvent2
functions.signature: int LiSendKeyboardEvent2(short keyCode, char keyAction, char modifiers, char flags);
functions.description: Extended keyboard event API allowing the client to mark unmapped/non-normalized keycodes using flags (Sunshine extension).
requirements: keyAction must be KEY_ACTION_DOWN or KEY_ACTION_UP.
modifiers is a bitmask of MODIFIER_* flags.
flags may include SS_KBE_FLAG_NON_NORMALIZED to indicate non-normalized keycode semantics.
keyCode must be a valid VK code for intended behavior.

functions.name: LiSendUtf8TextEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendUtf8TextEvent(const char *text, unsigned int length);
functions.description: Queues UTF-8 encoded text input for the remote host.
requirements: text must point to a buffer containing UTF-8 data; length specifies the number of bytes to send.
An active connection must exist for delivery (implicit).

functions.name: LiSendControllerEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendControllerEvent(int buttonFlags, unsigned char leftTrigger, unsigned char rightTrigger, short leftStickX, short leftStickY, short rightStickX, short rightStickY);
functions.description: Queues a single-controller gamepad state update to the host (controller 0).
requirements: buttonFlags is a bitfield of controller button flags (A/B/X/Y, dpad, shoulders, sticks, special, and extended flags where supported).
Trigger values are 0x00–0xFF; stick axes are signed shorts.
Assumes a single controller; for multi-controller scenarios use LiSendMultiControllerEvent().

functions.name: LiSendMultiControllerEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendMultiControllerEvent(short controllerNumber, short activeGamepadMask, int buttonFlags, unsigned char leftTrigger, unsigned char rightTrigger, short leftStickX, short leftStickY, short rightStickX, short rightStickY);
functions.description: Queues a gamepad event for a specific controller index with a mask of active controllers. Supports multiple controllers and indicates presence/removal via mask updates.
requirements: controllerNumber is zero-based; max 3 on GFE hosts and 15 on Sunshine hosts (indices beyond are invalid).
activeGamepadMask has bits set for each present controller; limited to 0x000F on GFE and 0xFFFF on Sunshine.
On generation 3 servers (GFE 2.1.x), events are sent as controller 0 regardless of controllerNumber.
To indicate arrival/removal, send an empty state update with the appropriate bit set/cleared; prefer LiSendControllerArrivalEvent() for arrivals.

functions.name: LiSendControllerArrivalEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendControllerArrivalEvent(uint8_t controllerNumber, uint16_t activeGamepadMask, uint8_t type, uint32_t supportedButtonFlags, uint16_t capabilities);
functions.description: Notifies the host of a newly available controller and its capabilities, allowing the host to choose an appropriate emulated controller. Falls back to LiSendMultiControllerEvent() if unsupported.
requirements: controllerNumber is zero-based; typical limits are 0–3 (GFE) or 0–15 (Sunshine).
activeGamepadMask indicates currently present controllers with bits set.
type should be LI_CTYPE_* (XBOX/PS/NINTENDO/UNKNOWN).
supportedButtonFlags is a bitmask of available controller buttons (same scheme as controller event flags).
capabilities is a bitmask of LI_CCAP_* (e.g., ANALOG_TRIGGERS, RUMBLE, TRIGGER_RUMBLE, TOUCHPAD, ACCEL, GYRO, BATTERY_STATE, RGB_LED).

functions.name: LiSendControllerTouchEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendControllerTouchEvent(uint8_t controllerNumber, uint8_t eventType, uint32_t pointerId, float x, float y, float pressure);
functions.description: Sends touchpad-associated touch events for a controller (e.g., DualShock/DualSense touchpad). Returns LI_ERR_UNSUPPORTED if the host does not support controller touch events.
requirements: controllerNumber is zero-based controller index.
eventType must be one of LI_TOUCH_EVENT_* constants.
pointerId must uniquely identify an active touch on the controller touchpad.
x and y are normalized [0.0, 1.0] over the video area (touchpad mapping); pressure in 0.0–1.0; use 0.0 for unknown.
Check support via LiGetHostFeatureFlags() for LI_FF_CONTROLLER_TOUCH_EVENTS.

functions.name: LiSendControllerMotionEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendControllerMotionEvent(uint8_t controllerNumber, uint8_t motionType, float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Sends motion sensor data for a controller. Report accelerometer in m/s^2 (including gravity) and gyroscope in deg/s. Hosts may request enablement via ConnListenerSetMotionEventState().
requirements: controllerNumber is zero-based controller index.
motionType must be LI_MOTION_TYPE_ACCEL or LI_MOTION_TYPE_GYRO.
Units: accelerometer x/y/z in m/s^2 (including gravity); gyroscope x/y/z in deg/s.
For power/performance, only send if host requested via ConnListenerSetMotionEventState().

functions.name: LiSendControllerBatteryEvent
functions.signature: int LiSendControllerBatteryEvent(uint8_t controllerNumber, uint8_t batteryState, uint8_t batteryPercentage);
functions.description: Sends the battery state/percentage for a controller so the host can mirror it in the emulated controller.
requirements: batteryState must be a LI_BATTERY_STATE_* constant.
batteryPercentage is 0–100 or LI_BATTERY_PERCENTAGE_UNKNOWN (0xFF).

functions.name: LiSendScrollEvent
functions.description: Queues a vertical mouse wheel scroll event where each click maps to WHEEL_DELTA (120) units on the host.
requirements: scrollClicks is a signed count of detents (clicks); host will multiply by 120.
Use LiSendHighResScrollEvent() for sub-120 unit scrolling.

functions.name: LiSendHighResScrollEvent
functions.description: Queues a high-resolution vertical scroll event allowing values smaller than 120 units for precision devices.
requirements: scrollAmount is a signed value representing wheel delta units directly (not limited to multiples of 120).

functions.name: LiSendHScrollEvent
functions.description: Queues a horizontal scroll event analogous to LiSendScrollEvent() (Sunshine extension).
requirements: scrollClicks is a signed count of detents (clicks).

functions.name: LiSendHighResHScrollEvent
functions.description: Queues a high-resolution horizontal scroll event analogous to LiSendHighResScrollEvent() (Sunshine extension).
requirements: scrollAmount is a signed value representing horizontal wheel delta units directly.

functions.name: LiGetMicroseconds
functions.description: Returns a timestamp in microseconds with an implementation-defined epoch. Only meaningful for relative comparisons with other values from this function.
requirements: Do not assume any epoch; only compare deltas between calls to LiGetMicroseconds().

functions.name: LiGetMillis
functions.description: Returns a timestamp in milliseconds with an implementation-defined epoch. Only meaningful for relative comparisons with other values from this function.
requirements: Do not assume any epoch; only compare deltas between calls to LiGetMillis().

functions.name: LiFindExternalAddressIP4
functions.signature: int LiFindExternalAddressIP4(const char* stunServer, unsigned short stunPort, unsigned int* wanAddr);
functions.description: Performs a simple STUN query to discover the WAN IPv4 address of the local machine, returning the address in network byte order.
requirements: stunServer must be a resolvable STUN server hostname.
stunPort is the UDP port of the STUN server.
wanAddr must be a valid writable pointer; on success it receives the IPv4 address in network byte order.

functions.name: LiGetPendingVideoFrames
functions.description: Returns the number of queued video frames waiting for delivery in push-based mode. Not relevant if CAPABILITY_DIRECT_SUBMIT is set for the video renderer.
requirements: Meaningful only when the video renderer does not set CAPABILITY_DIRECT_SUBMIT.
An active connection should be in progress for non-zero counts (implicit).

functions.name: LiGetPendingAudioFrames
functions.description: Returns the number of queued audio frames waiting for delivery in push-based mode. Prefer LiGetPendingAudioDuration() for duration-agnostic logic.
requirements: Meaningful only when the audio renderer does not set CAPABILITY_DIRECT_SUBMIT.
An active connection should be in progress for non-zero counts (implicit).

functions.name: LiGetPendingAudioDuration
functions.description: Returns the pending audio queue duration in milliseconds, independent of negotiated frame duration.
requirements: Meaningful only when the audio renderer does not set CAPABILITY_DIRECT_SUBMIT.
An active connection should be in progress for non-zero values (implicit).

functions.name: LiGetRTPAudioStats
functions.description: Returns a pointer to read-only statistics for the RTP audio stream (packet counts, FEC, OOS, invalid).
requirements: The returned structure must be treated as read-only; do not modify.
Statistics are meaningful during/after an active stream (implicit).

functions.name: LiGetRTPVideoStats
functions.description: Returns a pointer to read-only statistics for the RTP video stream (packet counts, FEC, OOS, invalid).
requirements: The returned structure must be treated as read-only; do not modify.
Statistics are meaningful during/after an active stream (implicit).

functions.name: LiGetPortFlagsFromStage
functions.description: Maps a connection stage code to a bitmask of ML_PORT_FLAG_* values likely involved if that stage fails, for targeted connectivity testing.
requirements: stage should be a STAGE_* constant. Returns 0 if no ports are implicated.

functions.name: LiGetPortFlagsFromTerminationErrorCode
functions.description: Maps a termination error code to a bitmask of ML_PORT_FLAG_* values likely involved in the failure, for targeted connectivity testing.
requirements: errorCode may be ML_ERROR_* or other codes documented by the library. Returns 0 if no ports are implicated.

functions.name: LiGetProtocolFromPortFlagIndex
functions.description: Returns the IP protocol (e.g., IPPROTO_TCP/IPPROTO_UDP) corresponding to a port index constant (ML_PORT_INDEX_*).
requirements: portFlagIndex must be one of the ML_PORT_INDEX_* constants.

functions.name: LiGetPortFromPortFlagIndex
functions.description: Returns the numeric port corresponding to a port index constant (ML_PORT_INDEX_*).
requirements: portFlagIndex must be one of the ML_PORT_INDEX_* constants.

functions.name: LiStringifyPortFlags
functions.signature: void LiStringifyPortFlags(unsigned int portFlags, const char* separator, char* outputBuffer, int outputBufferLength);
functions.description: Writes a delimited string representation of a ML_PORT_FLAG_* bitmask into the provided buffer. Subsequent entries are prefixed by the separator if provided. Output is truncated if the buffer is too small.
requirements: outputBuffer must be a valid writable buffer of size outputBufferLength bytes.
outputBufferLength should be > 0 to receive any output.
separator may be NULL to omit separators.

functions.name: LiTestClientConnectivity
functions.signature: unsigned int LiTestClientConnectivity(const char* testServer, unsigned short referencePort, unsigned int testPortFlags);
functions.description: Tests whether the local network permits connectivity on specified Moonlight ports by communicating with a remote test server. Returns 0 if all tested ports validate, ML_TEST_RESULT_INCONCLUSIVE on catastrophic error, or a bitmask of failed ML_PORT_FLAG_* values.
requirements: testServer must be a reachable Internet host running the compatible test server (see https://github.com/cgutman/gfe-loopback).
referencePort should be a commonly open TCP port (e.g., 80/443) to sanity-check reachability.
testPortFlags should be ML_PORT_FLAG_* bitmask (prefer ML_PORT_FLAG_ALL or values from LiGetPortFlagsFromStage()).

functions.name: LiWaitForNextVideoFrame
functions.description: Blocks until a video frame is available and dequeues it for pull-based rendering. Returns a handle and decode unit. Must be paired with LiCompleteVideoFrame() when processing is finished.
requirements: Only valid if the video renderer has CAPABILITY_PULL_RENDERER set.
frameHandle and decodeUnit must be valid writable pointers.
Caller must later invoke LiCompleteVideoFrame(*frameHandle, drStatus) with DR_* status for the processed frame.
Do not mix with push-based callbacks in the same renderer (mutually exclusive per capability).

functions.name: LiPollNextVideoFrame
functions.description: Non-blocking dequeue of the next available video frame for pull-based rendering. Returns false if no frame is available. Must be paired with LiCompleteVideoFrame().
requirements: Only valid if the video renderer has CAPABILITY_PULL_RENDERER set.
frameHandle and decodeUnit must be valid writable pointers.
Caller must later invoke LiCompleteVideoFrame(*frameHandle, drStatus).

functions.name: LiPeekNextVideoFrame
functions.description: Peeks at the next video frame's decode unit without dequeuing or obtaining a frame handle. Useful for inspection in pull-based mode.
requirements: Only valid if the video renderer has CAPABILITY_PULL_RENDERER set.
decodeUnit must be a valid writable pointer.
No LiCompleteVideoFrame() call is performed for peeks.

functions.name: LiWakeWaitForVideoFrame
functions.description: Wakes any threads blocked in LiWaitForNextVideoFrame(), typically to shut down or reconfigure the pull-based renderer.
requirements: Intended for use with CAPABILITY_PULL_RENDERER and threads waiting on LiWaitForNextVideoFrame().

functions.name: LiCompleteVideoFrame
functions.description: Signals completion of processing for a dequeued video frame obtained from LiWaitForNextVideoFrame() or LiPollNextVideoFrame(), providing the DR_* status (e.g., DR_OK or DR_NEED_IDR).
requirements: handle must be the VIDEO_FRAME_HANDLE obtained from a prior successful Wait/Poll call.
drStatus must be a valid DR_* status code (DR_OK or DR_NEED_IDR).
Only valid if the video renderer has CAPABILITY_PULL_RENDERER set.

functions.name: LiGetCurrentHostDisplayHdrMode
functions.description: Returns the last reported HDR on/off state of the host display, as communicated via ConnListenerSetHdrMode().
requirements: Meaningful after the host has reported HDR mode at least once via callbacks (implicit).

functions.name: LiGetHdrMetadata
functions.description: Fills the provided SS_HDR_METADATA with current HDR mastering metadata from the host display and content, when available. Valid only when HDR mode is active. Sunshine protocol extension.
requirements: metadata must be a valid writable pointer to SS_HDR_METADATA.
Call only when HDR mode is active on the host (see LiGetCurrentHostDisplayHdrMode() / ConnListenerSetHdrMode()).

functions.name: LiRequestIdrFrame
functions.description: Requests that the host send an IDR (key) frame soon. Useful if the client must reset decoder state without waiting to return DR_NEED_IDR on the next frame.
requirements: No guarantee that the next frame will be IDR; only that an IDR will arrive soon.

functions.name: LiGetHostFeatureFlags
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of extended features supported by the host (e.g., LI_FF_PEN_TOUCH_EVENTS, LI_FF_CONTROLLER_TOUCH_EVENTS).
requirements: Interpret bits using LI_FF_* constants to gate usage of optional APIs like touch/pen/controller touch events.

functions.name: xml_search
functions.signature: int xml_search(char* data, size_t len, char* node, char** result);
functions.description: Searches an XML buffer for a node and returns the node’s value or content via an output parameter. Intended for parsing Moonlight Embedded XML responses to extract a specific node identified by name. Return value semantics are not documented in this header; success/failure codes are unknown.
requirements: data must point to a readable memory buffer containing XML text of at least len bytes.
len must be the size of the XML buffer referenced by data.
node must be a non-null, null-terminated C string naming the XML node to search for.
result must be a non-null pointer to a char* variable to receive the located content pointer.
Ownership/lifetime of the memory referenced by *result is unknown from this header; do not assume the caller should free it without further documentation.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not specified.

functions.name: xml_applist
functions.signature: int xml_applist(char* data, size_t len, PAPP_LIST *app_list);
functions.description: Parses an XML buffer to produce a linked list of applications, returning the list head via app_list. Each list element contains an application name and id using the APP_LIST structure. Commonly used to interpret Moonlight Embedded app list responses. Return value semantics are not documented in this header; success/failure codes are unknown.
requirements: data must point to a readable memory buffer containing XML text of at least len bytes.
len must be the size of the XML buffer referenced by data.
app_list must be a non-null pointer to receive the head of a newly constructed APP_LIST linked list.
The memory allocation/ownership model for the returned list is not specified here; freeing responsibilities and API to release memory are unknown without additional documentation.
Input state of *app_list prior to the call is unspecified; do not assume it must be NULL based on this header alone.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not specified.

functions.name: xml_modelist
functions.signature: int xml_modelist(char* data, size_t len, PDISPLAY_MODE *mode_list);
functions.description: Parses an XML buffer to produce a linked list of display modes, returning the list head via mode_list. Each element uses DISPLAY_MODE with width, height, and refresh fields. Intended to parse Moonlight Embedded display mode listings. Return value semantics are not documented in this header; success/failure codes are unknown.
requirements: data must point to a readable memory buffer containing XML text of at least len bytes.
len must be the size of the XML buffer referenced by data.
mode_list must be a non-null pointer to receive the head of a newly constructed DISPLAY_MODE linked list.
The memory allocation/ownership model for the returned list is not specified here; freeing responsibilities and API to release memory are unknown without additional documentation.
Input state of *mode_list prior to the call is unspecified; do not assume it must be NULL based on this header alone.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not specified.

functions.name: xml_status
functions.description: Parses an XML buffer to obtain a status value from the document. Likely used to read a status code or boolean from Moonlight Embedded XML responses. Exact meaning and return conventions are not documented in this header; details are unknown.
requirements: data must point to a readable memory buffer containing XML text of at least len bytes.
len must be the size of the XML buffer referenced by data.
Interpretation of the returned int is unspecified in this header; callers must consult implementation or external documentation.

# We therefore craft an encoded blob that concatenates multiple interesting strings separated by NULs.
# The harness typically consumes sequential FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME calls from the same input stream.
# We will provide a sequence of strings covering:
# - Valid hostnames (DNS labels, mixed case, hyphens)
# - IPv4 literals
# - IPv6 literals (with and without brackets)
# - Internationalized domain names (unicode + punycode-like ascii fallback)
# - Local/reserved names
# - A plausible file path for keyDirectory (POSIX and Windows variants)
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

DNS_LABEL_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-'


def rand_label(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=20) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(r.choice(DNS_LABEL_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid starting/ending with hyphen per RFC
    if s and s[0] == '-':
        s = 'a' + s[1:]
    if s and s[-1] == '-':
        s = s[:-1] + 'b'
    return s


def gen_dns_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # 1-5 labels
    count = r.randint(1, 5)
    labels = [rand_label(r, 1, r.randint(3, 12)) for _ in range(count)]
    # Randomly mix case
    host = '.'.join(labels)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        host = ''.join(ch.upper() if r.random() < 0.3 else ch for ch in host)
    return host


def gen_ipv4(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer public/doc ranges and typical private ranges to hit code paths
    choices = [
        (192, 0, 2, r.randint(1, 254)),    # TEST-NET-1
        (198, 51, 100, r.randint(1, 254)), # TEST-NET-2
        (203, 0, 113, r.randint(1, 254)),  # TEST-NET-3
        (10, r.randint(0, 255), r.randint(0, 255), r.randint(1, 254)),
        (172, r.randint(16, 31), r.randint(0, 255), r.randint(1, 254)),
        (192, 168, r.randint(0, 255), r.randint(1, 254)),
        (127, 0, 0, 1),
    ]
    a, b, c, d = r.choice(choices)
    return f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"


def gen_ipv6(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a compressed IPv6 literal
    hextets = [f"{r.randint(0, 0xFFFF):x}" for _ in range(8)]
    # Insert a zero run to allow compression
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        i = r.randint(0, 6)
        run_len = r.randint(1, 7 - i)
        for j in range(i, i + run_len):
            hextets[j] = '0'
    # Compress the longest zero run manually
    # Find longest zero run
    best_i = -1
    best_len = 0
    i = 0
    while i < 8:
        if hextets[i] == '0':
            j = i
            while j < 8 and hextets[j] == '0':
                j += 1
            if j - i > best_len:
                best_len = j - i
                best_i = i
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    if best_len > 1:
        parts = []
        parts.extend(hextets[:best_i])
        parts.append('')
        parts.extend(hextets[best_i + best_len:])
        # Ensure proper placement of empty for :: at ends
        if parts and parts[0] == '':
            txt = ':' + ':'.join(parts)
        else:
            txt = ':'.join(parts)
        if txt.endswith(':'):
            txt += ':'
    else:
        txt = ':'.join(hextets)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # Bracketed form common in URLs (even though spec says no scheme here, some code handles brackets)
        return f"[{txt}]"
    return txt


def gen_idn(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Use some unicode letters and hyphens, then dot labels
    # Provide ASCII punycode-like fallback as well
    unicode_labels = [
        'münchen', '東京', 'пример', 'παράδειγμα', 'مثال', 'δοκιμή', '例子', '例え', '실례'
    ]
    label = r.choice(unicode_labels)
    ascii_fallback = 'xn--' + ''.join(ch for ch in label if ch.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))[:10]
    # Compose mixed labels
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return f"{label}.example"
    else:
        return f"{ascii_fallback}.{gen_dns_name(r)}"


def gen_local_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(['localhost', 'gateway.lan', 'router.local', 'nas.home', 'printer.office'])


def gen_path_posix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # plausible key directory
    parts = ['/', 'home', 'fuzz']
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append('keys')
    parts.append('moonlight')
    return '/'.join([parts[0]] + parts[1:])


def gen_path_windows(r: random.Random) -> str:
    drive = r.choice(list(string.ascii_uppercase)) + ':'
    comps = ['\\', 'Users', 'Fuzz', 'AppData', 'Local', 'Moonlight']
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        comps.append('Keys')
    return drive + '\\' + '\\'.join(comps[1:])


def gen_host_set(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    hosts = []
    # Ensure diversity and validity
    hosts.append(gen_dns_name(r))
    hosts.append(gen_ipv4(r))
    hosts.append(gen_ipv6(r))
    hosts.append(gen_local_name(r))
    hosts.append(gen_idn(r))
    # Add a couple more random DNS
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        hosts.append(gen_dns_name(r))
    return hosts


def gen_filename_set(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # Include both POSIX and Windows style paths
    names.append(gen_path_posix(r))
    names.append(gen_path_windows(r))
    # Also include a relative directory
    rel = 'keys_' + ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
    names.append(rel)
    return names


def assemble_cstring_pool(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated C strings; add a final NUL to terminate the last string
    data = b''
    for s in strings:
        # Limit individual string length to keep total under cap
        bs = s.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')[:512]
        data += bs + b'\x00'
    # Ensure at least one extra NUL padding
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    items: List[str] = []

    # For LiFindExternalAddressIP4 and LiTestClientConnectivity: host strings
    items.extend(gen_host_set(r))

    # For gs_init: address and keyDirectory filename path
    # Address can reuse host set; add another to vary
    items.append(gen_dns_name(r))

    # keyDirectory for gs_init via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
    items.extend(gen_filename_set(r))

    # For SERVER_INFORMATION fields: address, versions, rtsp URL path-like (without scheme)
    items.append(gen_dns_name(r))
    # Versions: simple semantic versions and strings
    ver_major = f"{r.randint(1, 10)}.{r.randint(0, 99)}.{r.randint(0, 999)}"
    ver_minor = f"GFE {r.randint(2, 10)}.{r.randint(0, 99)}"
    items.append(ver_major)
    items.append(ver_minor)
    # rtsp session URL tail (no scheme per description, but plausible path/query)
    sess = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(8))
    items.append(f"rtsp/session/{sess}?codec=h264&mode=lowlatency")

    # Include some duplicates to test internal caching/dup handling
    if items:
        items.append(items[0])

    blob = assemble_cstring_pool(items)
    # Truncate if necessary to MAX_TOTAL
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: delimiter string
# Used by LiStringifyPortFlags() as the separator argument. The fuzzer stub passes
# either a C-string (if length is even) or NULL (if odd). We want to generate
# interesting, valid short separator strings that exercise different parsing paths:
# - common delimiters (", ", ",", "; ", "|", "/", "\\", ":", "-", "_", ".")
# - whitespace variants (" ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n")
# - multi-byte UTF-8 delimiters (em dash, bullet, middot, non-breaking space)
# - empty string (length 0) – but note: the stub will only use the separator when
#   sepStr.size() is even. We include empty to hit the even-length branch with "".
# - repeated characters of varying even lengths
# - unusual punctuation and mixed sequences
#
# The generate(seed) function returns bytes to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR so that
# the C++ stub receives deterministic yet diverse separators.

COMMON_SEPARATORS: List[str] = [
    ", ", ",", "; ", ";", "|", "/", "\\", ":", "-", "_", ".", "::", " | ",
]
WHITESPACE_SEPARATORS: List[str] = [
    " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n", "\t|\t", " \t ",
]
UTF8_SEPARATORS: List[str] = [
    "\u2014",   # em dash —
    "\u2022",  # bullet •
    "\u00B7",  # middot ·
    "\u00A0",  # non-breaking space
    "\u2502",  # box drawings light vertical │
]

# Build patterned even-length strings
def patterned_separators(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    chars = [",", ";", "|", ":", " ", "-", "_", ".", "/", "\\"]
    out = []
    # Repeated single char (ensure even length)
    for ch in chars:
        n = rng.choice([2, 4, 6, 8])
        out.append(ch * n)
    # Mixed pairs
    pairs = [(",", " "), (";", " "), ("|", " "), (":", " "), ("-", ">"), ("<", ">"), ("(", ")")]
    for a, b in pairs:
        n = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4])
        out.append((a + b) * n)
    return out

# Compose a diverse pool of candidates and pick one with even length most of the time
# because the stub only uses the string when size() is even; otherwise it passes NULL.
# However, sometimes we intentionally return odd-length to exercise the NULL path.

def pick_separator(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pool: List[str] = []
    pool.extend(COMMON_SEPARATORS)
    pool.extend(WHITESPACE_SEPARATORS)
    pool.extend(UTF8_SEPARATORS)
    pool.extend(patterned_separators(rng))

    # Add some custom random small strings
    def rand_ascii(min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
        alphabet = ",;|:/-_ .\t\n\r" + string.punctuation
        L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
        return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(L))

    for _ in range(6):
        s = rand_ascii(1, 6)
        pool.append(s)

    # Include empty string (even length = 0) to test no-separator join
    pool.append("")

    # Bias towards even-length strings (~80%) to ensure separator is used often.
    want_even = rng.random() < 0.8

    if want_even:
        even_candidates = [s for s in pool if len(s.encode('utf-8')) % 2 == 0]
        # Fallback if none (shouldn't happen): adjust by appending a space
        if not even_candidates:
            s = rng.choice(pool)
            if len(s.encode('utf-8')) % 2 != 0:
                s += " "
            return s
        return rng.choice(even_candidates)
    else:
        odd_candidates = [s for s in pool if len(s.encode('utf-8')) % 2 == 1]
        if not odd_candidates:
            s = rng.choice(pool)
            if len(s.encode('utf-8')) % 2 == 0:
                s += "."  # make it odd
            return s
        return rng.choice(odd_candidates)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    sep = pick_separator(rng)
    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes (always small here)
    return sep.encode('utf-8')

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Target fuzzers use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to obtain paths for:
# - http_init: needs a directory path that exists and contains certificate/key files (client.pem/key.pem) inferred, but stub only needs directory to exist; http_init may read certs.
# - mkcert_save: needs three file paths to write cert, p12, and key. Paths should be valid and writable; directories must exist.
# - gs_init: keyDirectory path where keys may live; directory should exist. address path is via FUZZ_PARAM_STR, not our concern here.
# Therefore we will generate a bytes buffer that encodes a small virtual file layout description that the fuzzer harness will mirror to disk before using FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# However, since the framework provides FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME by creating a temp file and giving its path, we can only influence initial seed buffer contents.
# We will emit a newline-delimited list of intended paths plus directives to create directories and placeholder files. Many fuzz harnesses parse these patterns.
# Format we output:
# DIR:<path>
# FILE:<path>:<contents-hex>
# The buffer will contain a minimal, consistent set:
# - A base directory dirN with subdirs certs/, out/.
# - In certs/: client.pem and key.pem with plausible PEM headers.
# - In out/: placeholders for certFile, p12File, keyPairFile (may be overwritten).
# This increases chance that FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME returns paths within existing dirs.

MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 4096

PEM_CERT = (
    "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n"
    "MIIBszCCAVugAwIBAgIUAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEwDQYJ\n"
    "KoZIhvcNAQELBQAwFDESMBAGA1UEAwwJTW9ja0NlcnQwHhcNMjAwMTAxMDAwMDAw\n"
    "WhcNNDAwMTAxMDAwMDAwWjAUMRIwEAYDVQQDDAlNb2NrQ2VydDCBnzANBgkqhkiG\n"
    "9w0BAQEFAAOBjQAwgYkCgYEAzBk7mI7t6L7v1L8y1k2n5N0tN1q2X8p1r3cGQ1Kc\n"
    "b2c62r8m2hQ1b1y3U1m3q2eQXxq1m9s7y0f0r3m3c2l1p0o9n8m7l6k5j4i3h2g1f\n"
    "eW5hbGxxdWVQbGFjZWhvbGRlcg==\n"
    "-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
)

PEM_KEY = (
    "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
    "MIIBVwIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCAT8wggE7AgEAAkEAzBk7mI7t6L7v1L8y\n"
    "1k2n5N0tN1q2X8p1r3cGQ1Kcb2c62r8m2hQ1b1y3U1m3q2eQXxq1m9s7y0f0r3m3\n"
    "c2wIDAQAB\n"
    "-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
)

# Simple helper to make a safe path component

def rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len=5, max_len=10) -> str:
    s = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_", k=rng.randint(min_len, max_len)))
    # avoid leading dot to reduce hidden files
    if s.startswith('.'):
        s = 'x' + s[1:]
    return s


def build_layout(seed: int) -> List[str]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    base = rand_component(rng, 6, 12)
    # choose platform-ish root indicator keywords; harness often maps relative paths under temp
    root = base
    cert_dir = os.path.join(root, 'certs')
    out_dir = os.path.join(root, 'out')

    entries: List[str] = []
    # Directories
    for d in [root, cert_dir, out_dir]:
        entries.append(f"DIR:{d}")

    # Required for http_init per header notes: client.pem and key.pem in keyDirectory
    client_pem_path = os.path.join(cert_dir, 'client.pem')
    key_pem_path = os.path.join(cert_dir, 'key.pem')

    # Placeholders for mkcert_save outputs; randomize names to diversify
    cert_out = os.path.join(out_dir, rand_component(rng) + '.crt')
    p12_out = os.path.join(out_dir, rand_component(rng) + '.p12')
    key_out = os.path.join(out_dir, rand_component(rng) + '.key')

    # Files with plausible contents
    entries.append(f"FILE:{client_pem_path}:{PEM_CERT.encode('utf-8').hex()}")
    entries.append(f"FILE:{key_pem_path}:{PEM_KEY.encode('utf-8').hex()}")

    # Also include an XML file that could be consumed by XML parsers in other fuzzers
    xml_dir = os.path.join(root, 'xml')
    entries.append(f"DIR:{xml_dir}")
    # A small but valid app list XML
    app_xml = (
        "<root>\n"
        "  <status>200</status>\n"
        "  <apps>\n"
        "    <app><name>Minecraft</name><id>1</id></app>\n"
        "    <app><name>Portal 2</name><id>2</id></app>\n"
        "  </apps>\n"
        "</root>\n"
    )
    entries.append(f"FILE:{os.path.join(xml_dir, 'apps.xml')}:{app_xml.encode('utf-8').hex()}")

    # Pre-create empty outputs that are writable/overwriteable
    for p in [cert_out, p12_out, key_out]:
        entries.append(f"FILE:{p}:")

    # Provide a "keyDirectory" hint file listing, so harness could pick cert_dir as a directory source
    entries.append(f"HINT:keyDirectory={cert_dir}")
    # Provide three filename hints for mkcert_save
    entries.append(f"HINT:certFile={cert_out}")
    entries.append(f"HINT:p12File={p12_out}")
    entries.append(f"HINT:keyPairFile={key_out}")

    # Ensure total size limit
    blob = "\n".join(entries).encode('utf-8')
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        # Trim optional XML or hints if oversized
        trimmed = [e for e in entries if not e.startswith('FILE:') or not e.endswith('apps.xml:'+app_xml.encode('utf-8').hex())]
        blob = "\n".join(trimmed).encode('utf-8')
    return entries


def serialize_entries(entries: List[str]) -> bytes:
    return ("\n".join(entries) + "\n").encode('utf-8')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries = build_layout(seed)

    # Randomly add a few alternate directory names to diversify FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME pool
    extra_dirs = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(extra_dirs):
        d = os.path.join(entries[0].split(':',1)[1], rand_component(rng)) if entries else rand_component(rng)
        entries.append(f"DIR:{d}")

    # Randomly duplicate key files under alternate names some code might look for
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        alt_client = entries[1].split(':',1)[1]  # path after DIR:root
        certs_dir = os.path.dirname(alt_client)
        alt_name = 'certificate.pem'
        entries.append(f"FILE:{os.path.join(certs_dir, alt_name)}:{PEM_CERT.encode('utf-8').hex()}")

    buf = serialize_entries(entries)
    # Enforce max size
    return buf[:MAX_TOTAL_BYTES]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets FUZZ_PARAM_STR() used to populate SERVER_INFORMATION fields:
# - address: Prefer valid hostnames/IPs
# - serverInfoAppVersion/serverInfoGfeVersion: semantic version strings
# - rtspSessionUrl: plausible RTSP/HTTP(S) URL
# The fuzzer will request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values sequentially from the same buffer.
# We'll pack them as length-prefixed UTF-8 strings so the harness can split them deterministically.
# Format:
#   [count:1]
#   repeat count times: [len:2 little-endian][bytes]
# Keep total <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _le16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF))


def _choose_host(r: random.Random) -> str:
    kinds = ["ipv4", "hostname", "fqdn", "ipv6"]
    k = r.choice(kinds)
    if k == "ipv4":
        # Avoid 0.0.0.0; include private, loopback, public-like
        octets = [
            r.randint(1, 223),
            r.randint(0, 255),
            r.randint(0, 255),
            r.randint(1, 254),
        ]
        return ".".join(map(str, octets))
    if k == "ipv6":
        # Compressed or full
        def group():
            return f"{r.randint(0, 0xFFFF):x}"
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            return ":".join(group() for _ in range(8))
        # simple compression with one ::
        left = ":".join(group() for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)))
        right = ":".join(group() for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)))
        return f"{left}::{right}"
    if k == "fqdn":
        labels = []
        nlabels = r.randint(2, 4)
        for i in range(nlabels):
            ln = r.randint(1, 12)
            s = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(ln))
            labels.append(s)
        tld = r.choice(["com", "net", "org", "io", "local", "lan"])
        return ".".join(labels + [tld])
    # hostname (single label or with dash)
    base = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10)))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        base += "-" + ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)))
    return base


def _semver(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate semantic version-like strings covering diverse patterns
    patterns: List[str] = []
    major = str(r.randint(0, 99))
    minor = str(r.randint(0, 99))
    patch = str(r.randint(0, 999))
    build = str(r.randint(1, 9999))
    pre = r.choice(["alpha", "beta", "rc"])
    pre_num = str(r.randint(1, 10))
    patterns.append(f"{major}.{minor}")
    patterns.append(f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}")
    patterns.append(f"v{major}.{minor}")
    patterns.append(f"v{major}.{minor}.{patch}")
    patterns.append(f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}-{pre}{pre_num}")
    patterns.append(f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}+build.{build}")
    patterns.append(f"{major}")
    # Occasionally include vendor-like strings
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        vendor = r.choice(["GFE", "Sunshine", "Moonlight", "NV", "Shield"])    
        patterns.append(f"{vendor} {major}.{minor}.{patch}")
    return r.choice(patterns)


def _rtsp_or_http_url(r: random.Random, host: str) -> str:
    # Produce plausible RTSP or HTTP(S) URLs that a client might store
    scheme = r.choice(["rtsp", "rtspu", "rtsp-over-http", "http", "https"]) if \
        (":" not in host or r.random() < 0.6) else r.choice(["http", "https"])  # IPv6 often with http(s) unless bracketed

    # If IPv6, bracket it
    if ":" in host and not host.startswith("["):
        host_disp = f"[{host}]"
    else:
        host_disp = host

    default_ports = {
        "rtsp": 554,
        "rtspu": 554,
        "rtsp-over-http": 80,
        "http": 80,
        "https": 443,
    }
    port = default_ports[scheme]
    # Occasionally pick a non-default but common port
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        if scheme in ("http", "rtsp-over-http"):
            port = r.choice([80, 8000, 8080, 8888, 47989])
        elif scheme == "https":
            port = r.choice([443, 8443, 47984])
        else:  # rtsp/rtspu
            port = r.choice([554, 8554, 5544, 47998])

    # Paths commonly used
    paths = [
        "stream", "video", "live", "session", "gamestream", "rdp", "h264", "h265"
    ]
    qp_variants = [
        "", "?tcp", "?udp", "?transport=tcp", "?transport=udp", "?enableAudio=1", "?client=moonlight"
    ]
    path = r.choice(paths)
    qp = r.choice(qp_variants)

    return f"{scheme}://{host_disp}:{port}/{path}{qp}"


def _pack_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(len(strings) & 0xFF)
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')
        # enforce max length per entry to keep under MAX_TOTAL
        if len(b) > 1000:
            b = b[:1000]
        out += _le16(len(b))
        out += b
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate fields in the same order as the stub consumes FUZZ_PARAM_STR():
    # addr, ver1, ver2, rtsp
    host = _choose_host(r)
    addr = host

    ver1 = _semver(r)
    # Sometimes make app and gfe versions different to exercise comparisons

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for a binary blob used as frame segment data (e.g., SPS or generic NAL/bitstream chunks)
# The goal is to produce valid/interesting inputs for consumers like gs_sps_fix() that expect
# H.264 SPS NAL units or generic frame segment data. We focus on generating:
# - Raw H.264/AVC NAL units with start codes
# - Specifically SPS (nal_unit_type=7) with plausible bitstream fields
# - PPS (type=8), IDR slice (type=5), SEI (type=6), AUD (type=9)
# - Mixtures of Annex B start codes (3 or 4 bytes)
# - Optionally multiple concatenated NAL units to simulate typical streams
# Output limited to <= 2048 bytes for the stub, but cap at 1024 to stay well within limits

# Utilities for Exp-Golomb coding and RBSP/EBSP handling

def _ue(v: int) -> List[int]:
    # Unsigned Exp-Golomb to bit list (0/1 ints)
    if v < 0:
        v = 0
    code_num = v + 1
    bits = bin(code_num)[2:]
    prefix_zeros = len(bits) - 1
    out = [0] * prefix_zeros + [1]
    out += [int(b) for b in bits[1:]]
    return out

def _se(v: int) -> List[int]:
    # Signed Exp-Golomb
    if v == 0:
        code_num = 0
    elif v > 0:
        code_num = 2 * v - 1
    else:
        code_num = -2 * v
    return _ue(code_num)

def _bits(val: int, n: int) -> List[int]:
    return [((val >> (n-1-i)) & 1) for i in range(n)]

def _pack_bits_to_bytes(bits: List[int]) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    cur = 0
    cnt = 0
    for b in bits:
        cur = (cur << 1) | (b & 1)
        cnt += 1
        if cnt == 8:
            out.append(cur)
            cur = 0
            cnt = 0
    if cnt:
        out.append(cur << (8-cnt))
    return out

def _rbsp_trailing_bits(bits: List[int]) -> List[int]:
    # Append rbsp_stop_one_bit then pad to next byte boundary with zeros
    bits = bits[:] + [1]
    pad = (-len(bits)) & 7
    bits += [0] * pad
    return bits

def _ebsp_from_rbsp(rbsp: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Insert emulation prevention byte 0x03 after any 00 00 {00,01..03}
    out = bytearray()
    zero_count = 0
    for b in rbsp:
        if zero_count >= 2 and b <= 0x03:
            out.append(0x03)
            zero_count = 0
        out.append(b)
        if b == 0x00:
            zero_count += 1
        else:
            zero_count = 0
    return bytes(out)

def _annexb_start_code(four: bool) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00\x00\x00\x01" if four else b"\x00\x00\x01"

def _nal_header(nal_ref_idc: int, nal_unit_type: int) -> int:
    forbidden_zero_bit = 0
    return (forbidden_zero_bit << 7) | ((nal_ref_idc & 0x3) << 5) | (nal_unit_type & 0x1F)

def _gen_sps_bits(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    # Reasonable SPS defaults; vary profile/level/size
    profile_idc = rng.choice([66, 77, 100])  # BP, MP, High
    constraint_set_flags = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 6)  # 6 bits of constraints
    level_idc = rng.choice([30, 31, 32, 40])
    seq_parameter_set_id = rng.randrange(0, 8)

    bits = []
    bits += _bits(profile_idc, 8)
    bits += _bits(constraint_set_flags, 8)  # includes reserved_zero_2bits
    bits += _bits(level_idc, 8)
    bits += _ue(seq_parameter_set_id)

    chroma_format_idc = 1
    if profile_idc in (100, 110, 122, 244, 44, 83, 86, 118, 128, 138, 139, 134):
        bits += _ue(chroma_format_idc)
        if chroma_format_idc == 3:
            bits += _bits(0, 1)  # separate_colour_plane_flag
        bits += _ue(8)  # bit_depth_luma_minus8
        bits += _ue(8)  # bit_depth_chroma_minus8
        bits += _bits(0, 1)  # qpprime_y_zero_transform_bypass_flag
        # seq_scaling_matrix_present_flag
        bits += _bits(0, 1)

    log2_max_frame_num_minus4 = rng.randrange(0, 12)
    bits += _ue(log2_max_frame_num_minus4)

    pic_order_cnt_type = rng.choice([0, 2])  # avoid type 1 complexity
    bits += _ue(pic_order_cnt_type)
    if pic_order_cnt_type == 0:
        bits += _ue(rng.randrange(0, 12))  # log2_max_pic_order_cnt_lsb_minus4
    else:
        # type 2: nothing else
        pass

    max_num_ref_frames = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    bits += _ue(max_num_ref_frames)
    bits += _bits(0, 1)  # gaps_in_frame_num_value_allowed_flag

    # Choose a common resolution; gs_sps_init(width,height) may expect sensible sizes
    width = rng.choice([1280, 1920, 2560, 3840])
    height = rng.choice([720, 1080, 1440, 2160])

    # Compute macroblock-aligned values
    pic_width_in_mbs_minus1 = width // 16 - 1
    # Assume frame_mbs_only_flag=1, no mb_adaptive_frame_field
    mbs_per_frame_row = height // 16
    pic_height_in_map_units_minus1 = mbs_per_frame_row - 1

    bits += _ue(pic_width_in_mbs_minus1)
    bits += _ue(pic_height_in_map_units_minus1)

    frame_mbs_only_flag = 1
    bits += _bits(frame_mbs_only_flag, 1)
    if not frame_mbs_only_flag:
        bits += _bits(0, 1)  # mb_adaptive_frame_field_flag
    bits += _bits(0, 1)  # direct_8x8_inference_flag

    # Crop occasionally to exercise fixups
    frame_cropping_flag = 1 if rng.random() < 0.3 else 0
    bits += _bits(frame_cropping_flag, 1)
    if frame_cropping_flag:
        # Use values that keep dimensions valid
        crop_unit_x = 1
        crop_unit_y = 2  # for 4:2:0
        # Make small crops
        left = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        right = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        top = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        bottom = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        bits += _ue(left)
        bits += _ue(right)
        bits += _ue(top)
        bits += _ue(bottom)

    vui_parameters_present_flag = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 0
    bits += _bits(vui_parameters_present_flag, 1)
    if vui_parameters_present_flag:
        # Provide minimal VUI: aspect_ratio_info_present_flag, timing_info, colorimetry sometimes
        bits += _bits(1, 1)  # aspect_ratio_info_present_flag
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            # common SARs
            sar_idc = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 255])
            bits += _bits(sar_idc, 8)
            if sar_idc == 255:
                bits += _bits(rng.randrange(1, 65535), 16)
                bits += _bits(rng.randrange(1, 65535), 16)
        else:
            bits += _bits(0, 1)  # aspect_ratio_info_present_flag = 0 (but we've written 1 already); keep simple by always 1
        bits += _bits(0, 1)  # overscan_info_present_flag
        bits += _bits(1 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 0, 1)  # video_signal_type_present_flag
        if bits[-1] == 1:
            bits += _bits(5, 3)  # video_format
            bits += _bits(0, 1)  # video_full_range_flag
            bits += _bits(1 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 0, 1)  # colour_description_present_flag
            if bits[-1] == 1:
                bits += _bits(rng.choice([1, 9, 10, 12]), 8)  # colour_primaries
                bits += _bits(rng.choice([1, 9, 10]), 8)      # transfer_characteristics
                bits += _bits(rng.choice([1, 9]), 8)          # matrix_coeffs
        bits += _bits(0, 1)  # chroma_loc_info_present_flag
        bits += _bits(1 if rng.random() < 0.8 else 0, 1)  # timing_info_present_flag
        if bits[-1] == 1:
            # Use common timing: 90kHz num_units_in_tick with time_scale 180k -> 50 fps, or 90k/ 2*90k -> 25fps
            num_units_in_tick = rng.choice([1001, 1000, 90000])
            time_scale = rng.choice([2002, 2000, 180000])
            fixed_frame_rate_flag = 1
            bits += _bits(num_units_in_tick, 32)
            bits += _bits(time_scale, 32)
            bits += _bits(fixed_frame_rate_flag, 1)

    return _rbsp_trailing_bits(bits)


def _build_sps_nal(rng: random.Random, four_byte_sc: bool) -> bytes:
    bits = _gen_sps_bits(rng)
    rbsp = _pack_bits_to_bytes(bits)
    ebsp = _ebsp_from_rbsp(rbsp)
    hdr = bytes([_nal_header(3, 7)])
    return _annexb_start_code(four_byte_sc) + hdr + ebsp


def _build_pps_nal(rng: random.Random, four_byte_sc: bool) -> bytes:
    bits: List[int] = []
    pps_id = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    sps_id = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    bits += _ue(pps_id)
    bits += _ue(sps_id)
    bits += _bits(rng.randrange(0, 2), 1)  # entropy_coding_mode_flag
    bits += _bits(0, 1)  # pic_order_present_flag
    # num_slice_groups_minus1
    bits += _ue(0)
    # num_ref_idx_l0_default_active_minus1 / l1
    bits += _ue(rng.randrange(0, 2))
    bits += _ue(rng.randrange(0, 2))
    bits += _se(0)  # weighted_pred flags simplified via defaults: skip, keep simple
    bits += _bits(0, 1)  # weighted_pred_flag
    bits += _bits(0, 2)  # weighted_bipred_idc
    bits += _se(0)       # pic_init_qp_minus26
    bits += _se(0)       # pic_init_qs_minus26
    bits += _se(0)       # chroma_qp_index_offset
    bits += _bits(1 if rng.random() < 0.3 else 0, 1)  # deblocking_filter_control_present_flag
    bits += _bits(0, 1)  # constrained_intra_pred_flag
    bits += _bits(0, 1)  # redundant_pic_cnt_present_flag
    bits = _rbsp_trailing_bits(bits)
    rbsp = _pack_bits_to_bytes(bits)
    ebsp = _ebsp_from_rbsp(rbsp)
    hdr = bytes([_nal_header(3, 8)])
    return _annexb_start_code(four_byte_sc) + hdr + ebsp


def _build_aud_nal(rng: random.Random, four_byte_sc: bool) -> bytes:
    primary_pic_type = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    # Exp-Golomb in SEI/AUD often byte-aligned with rbsp_trailing_bits; here keep it simple: 3-bit field + rbsp_trailing_bits
    bits = _bits(primary_pic_type, 3)
    bits = _rbsp_trailing_bits(bits)
    rbsp = _pack_bits_to_bytes(bits)
    ebsp = _ebsp_from_rbsp(rbsp)
    hdr = bytes([_nal_header(0, 9)])
    return _annexb_start_code(four_byte_sc) + hdr + ebsp


def _build_sei_nal(rng: random.Random, four_byte_sc: bool) -> bytes:
    # Build a simple buffering_period or pic_timing payload; keep generic: payload_type=5 (user_data_unregistered) with UUID and bytes
    payload_type = 5
    payload = bytearray()
    # 16-byte UUID
    payload += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
    # Some random payload bytes
    sz = rng.randrange(4, 32)
    payload += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(sz))
    # write payloadType and payloadSize with 0xFF continuation mechanism
    nal_payload = bytearray()
    pt = payload_type
    while pt >= 255:
        nal_payload.append(255)
        pt -= 255
    nal_payload.append(pt)
    size = len(payload)
    while size >= 255:
        nal_payload.append(255)
        size -= 255
    nal_payload.append(size)
    nal_payload += payload
    nal_payload.append(0x80)  # rbsp_trailing_bits (1) and pad
    hdr = bytes([_nal_header(0, 6)])
    return _annexb_start_code(four_byte_sc) + hdr + bytes(nal_payload)


def _build_idr_slice_stub(rng: random.Random, four_byte_sc: bool) -> bytes:
    # Minimal slice header for IDR with few bytes payload
    bits: List[int] = []
    bits += _ue(0)  # first_mb_in_slice
    bits += _ue(7)  # slice_type (I slice variants)
    bits += _ue(rng.randrange(0, 8))  # pic_parameter_set_id
    bits += _bits(rng.randrange(0, 256), 8)  # frame_num (approx; simplified)
    # idr_pic_id
    bits += _ue(rng.randrange(0, 4))
    bits = _rbsp_trailing_bits(bits)
    rbsp = _pack_bits_to_bytes(bits)
    ebsp = _ebsp_from_rbsp(rbsp)
    hdr = bytes([_nal_header(3, 5)])
    return _annexb_start_code(four_byte_sc) + hdr + ebsp + bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randrange(8, 32)))


def _compose_stream(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    # Decide start code length pattern
    four = rng.random() < 0.6

    # Build a sequence of NALs; ensure at least one SPS
    parts.append(_build_aud_nal(rng, four) if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"")
    parts.append(_build_sps_nal(rng, four))
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        parts.append(_build_pps_nal(rng, four))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_build_sei_nal(rng, four))
    # Optionally include an IDR slice stub
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(_build_idr_slice_stub(rng, four))

    blob = b"".join(p for p in parts if p)

    # Cap size to within fuzzer stub limit (<=2048); trim gracefully at NAL boundaries by dropping extras if needed
    if len(blob) > 1024:
        # attempt to drop from the tail until under limit
        while len(blob) > 1024:
            # remove last NAL by finding previous start code
            idx = blob.rfind(b"\x00\x00\x01")
            idx4 = blob.rfind(b"\x00\x00\x00\x01")
            idx = max(idx, idx4)
            if idx <= 0:
                break
            blob = blob[:idx]
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # With some probability, return a generic binary blob to exercise non-AnnexB consumers
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.15:
        size = rng.randrange(16, 256)
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
    else:
        return _compose_stream(rng)

import os
import random
from typing import List

# Data type: binary key (16 bytes)
# Target stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR twice to fill 16-byte AES key and 16-byte IV.
# Our generator should return a bytes buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR will consume.
# Typical fuzz harnesses split the provided buffer into successive FUZZ_PARAM_* consumptions.
# We'll therefore encode two 16-byte keys back-to-back, with some variability and edge-interesting patterns.

# Helper patterns commonly interesting for AES keys/IVs
_FIXED_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x00" * 16,                      # all zero
    b"\xff" * 16,                      # all 0xFF
    bytes(range(16)),                   # 00 01 02 ... 0F
    bytes([0x10] * 16),                # uniform non-zero
    b"0123456789ABCDEF",               # ASCII sequence 16 bytes
    b"ABCDEFGHabcdefgh",               # mixed case ASCII 16 bytes
    b"\x80" + b"\x00" * 15,           # MSB set then zeros
    b"\x00" * 15 + b"\x01",           # trailing one
]

# Produce a 16-byte key with structured randomness
def make_key(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if choice == 0:
        # Choose from fixed patterns
        return rng.choice(_FIXED_PATTERNS)
    elif choice == 1:
        # High entropy random
        return rng.randbytes(16)
    elif choice == 2:
        # Repeated 2-byte word
        w = rng.getrandbits(16)
        return int.to_bytes(w, 2, 'big') * 8
    elif choice == 3:
        # Alternating bytes
        a = rng.getrandbits(8)
        b = rng.getrandbits(8)
        return bytes([a, b] * 8)
    elif choice == 4:
        # Incrementing from random start modulo 256
        start = rng.getrandbits(8)
        return bytes([(start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(16)])
    else:
        # ASCII-visible but full 0-255 spread sometimes
        # Mix digits/letters with a few non-printables
        buf = bytearray()
        alphabet = b"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
        for i in range(16):
            if rng.random() < 0.15:
                buf.append(rng.getrandbits(8))
            else:
                buf.append(alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))])
        return bytes(buf)

# Some harnesses expect FUZZ_PARAM_STR to extract a length-prefixed blob or a null-terminated string.
# To remain valid regardless, we will provide exact 16-byte segments without embedded NUL constraints,
# but also sometimes include a terminating NUL to allow shorter-than-16 strings (the stub pads to 16).
# We'll compose two segments possibly separated by random delimiters that common fuzzers can parse:
# - Option A: [len16][16 bytes][len16][16 bytes]
# - Option B: [16 bytes]['\0'][16 bytes]['\0'] (C-strings)
# - Option C: Plain concatenation of two 16-byte blobs

def build_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    key = make_key(rng)
    iv = make_key(rng)

    mode = rng.randint(0, 2)
    if mode == 0:
        # Length-prefixed with 1-byte length (exact 16)
        return bytes([16]) + key + bytes([16]) + iv
    elif mode == 1:
        # Null-terminated C-strings (ensure no internal NULs if we want it to stop exactly)
        # But the stub will copy up to 16 and pad; having earlier NUL is fine. We'll craft printable to avoid early stop.
        def sanitize_ascii(b: bytes) -> bytes:
            # Replace NUL with 'A' to ensure full 16 before terminator
            if 0 in b:
                ba = bytearray(b)
                for i, v in enumerate(ba):
                    if v == 0:
                        ba[i] = 0x41
                return bytes(ba)
            return b
        key_s = sanitize_ascii(key)
        iv_s = sanitize_ascii(iv)
        return key_s + b"\x00" + iv_s + b"\x00"
    else:
        # Plain concatenation; many harnesses will split on demand
        return key + iv


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    payload = build_payload(rng)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]
    return payload

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate initial buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the xml_search fuzzer stub.
# The stub uses two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls:
#  - xmlBuf: Arbitrary XML-like buffer (readable bytes, length = size())
#  - nodeName: C string node name to search for (null-terminated by stub)
# Our generator should return a single bytes object; fuzzing harness will slice it
# to feed both FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We therefore pack both values into one buffer
# with a simple self-describing format so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR call can pull a
# contiguous interesting region. Typical harnesses provide the same initial buffer
# to each FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocation in order; to maximize usefulness regardless of
# consumption strategy, we place multiple XML documents and multiple node names.

# Design:
#  - Emit a concatenation of blocks: [XML doc]\0 [node name]\0 [XML doc]\0 [node name]\0 ...
#  - XML documents are valid/parsable-looking UTF-8 with typical constructs:
#      * XML declaration
#      * Root with namespaces occasionally
#      * Nested elements, attributes, text, CDATA, comments, self-closing tags
#      * Repeated and varying tag names to exercise search, including alphanumeric
#  - Node names are alphanumeric strings per data_type description; we also include
#    some that match tags/attributes in the XML to increase hit probability.
#  - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits


def _rand_alnum(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(n))


def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    return rng.choices(items, weights=weights, k=1)[0]


def _make_tag_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer alphanumeric, allow camelCase and digits as suffix
    base = _rand_alnum(rng, 3, 10)
    # Ensure starts with a letter per XML rules; if not, prefix with a letter
    if not base[0].isalpha():
        base = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) + base
    # Occasionally camelCase
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        pos = rng.randint(1, len(base)-1)
        base = base[:pos] + base[pos].upper() + base[pos+1:]
    return base


def _xml_escape(text: str) -> str:
    return (text.replace('&', '&')
                .replace('<', '<')
                .replace('>', '>')
                .replace('"', '"')
                .replace("'", '''))


def _make_element(rng: random.Random, tag: str, depth: int, known_tags: List[str]) -> str:
    # Attributes
    attrs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        aname = _make_tag_name(rng)
        aval = _rand_alnum(rng, 0, 12)
        attrs.append(f'{aname}="{_xml_escape(aval)}"')
        if aname not in known_tags and rng.random() < 0.1:
            known_tags.append(aname)  # allow searching attributes by name in some impls
    attr_str = (' ' + ' '.join(attrs)) if attrs else ''

    # Decide on element content
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.25:
        # Self-closing
        return f'<{tag}{attr_str}/>'
    elif roll < 0.55 and depth > 0:
        # Nested children
        children = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            ctag = _make_tag_name(rng)
            known_tags.append(ctag)
            children.append(_make_element(rng, ctag, depth-1, known_tags))
        inner = ''.join(children)
        return f'<{tag}{attr_str}>{inner}</{tag}>'
    elif roll < 0.8:
        # Text content
        text_len = rng.randint(0, 20)
        text = _rand_alnum(rng, text_len, text_len)
        return f'<{tag}{attr_str}>{_xml_escape(text)}</{tag}>'
    else:
        # Mixed content with CDATA and comment
        text1 = _rand_alnum(rng, 1, 8)
        text2 = _rand_alnum(rng, 1, 8)
        cdata = _rand_alnum(rng, 0, 10)
        return f'<{tag}{attr_str}>{_xml_escape(text1)}<![CDATA[{cdata}]]><!--{_xml_escape(text2)}--></{tag}>'


def _make_xml_doc(rng: random.Random, known_tags: List[str]) -> str:
    # Optional XML declaration
    decl = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        enc = _weighted_choice(rng, ['UTF-8', 'utf-8', 'UTF-16', 'us-ascii'], [6, 2, 1, 1])
        decl = f'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="{enc}"?>\n'

    # Optional comment or processing instruction
    preface = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        preface = f'<!--{_xml_escape(_rand_alnum(rng, 4, 24))}-->'
    elif rng.random() < 0.25:
        preface = f'<?proc {_make_tag_name(rng)}="{_xml_escape(_rand_alnum(rng, 0, 10))}"?>'

    root = _make_tag_name(rng)
    known_tags.append(root)

    # Optional namespace-ish attributes
    ns_attr = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        ns = _make_tag_name(rng).lower()
        ns_attr = f' xmlns:{ns}="http://example.com/{ns}"'

    # Build several children including duplicates to improve search hits
    children = []
    depth = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        tag = _make_tag_name(rng)
        known_tags.append(tag)
        children.append(_make_element(rng, tag, depth, known_tags))

    # Insert some repeated tag names
    if known_tags and rng.random() < 0.6:
        rep = rng.choice(known_tags)
        children.append(_make_element(rng, rep, depth, known_tags))

    body = ''.join(children)
    return f'{decl}{preface}<{root}{ns_attr}>{body}</{root}>'


def _make_node_names(rng: random.Random, known_tags: List[str], count: int) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # Include some known tags to ensure matches
    rng.shuffle(known_tags)
    for t in known_tags[: max(0, min(count, len(known_tags)) // 2)]:
        # Enforce alphanumeric per data type; strip non-alnum (should be none)
        t_clean = ''.join(ch for ch in t if ch.isalnum()) or 'a'
        names.append(t_clean)
    # Add random alnum names that may or may not exist
    while len(names) < count:
        names.append(_rand_alnum(rng, 1, 12))
    return names


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total_budget = 4096

    # We will build 2-5 XML docs and 2-5 node names interleaved
    doc_count = rng.randint(2, 5)

    known_tags: List[str] = []
    docs: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(doc_count):
        doc = _make_xml_doc(rng, known_tags)
        docs.append(doc)

    # Node names to pair with docs; aim for more names than docs
    name_count = rng.randint(doc_count, doc_count + 3)
    node_names = _make_node_names(rng, known_tags, name_count)

    # Interleave: [doc0]\0 [name0]\0 [doc1]\0 [name1]\0 ... then remaining names
    for i in range(max(doc_count, name_count)):
        if i < doc_count:
            b = docs[i].encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            parts.append(b + b'\x00')
        if i < name_count:
            nb = node_names[i].encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
            parts.append(nb + b'\x00')

    blob = b''.join(parts)
    if len(blob) > total_budget:
        # Trim safely at a boundary: cut and ensure trailing null terminator
        blob = blob[:total_budget-1] + b'\x00'

    # Ensure non-empty per FUZZ_PARAM_STR expectation (length >= 1)
    if not blob:
        blob = b'A\x00B\x00'

    return blob
